rv.q: From the opening beat, you can instantly feel the heat of this show’s originality.
Hamilton is a knockout, and its British cast is superb, with two star-making performances from Giles Terera and, in the title role, magnetic newcomer Jamael Westman.
Miranda's exhilarating, game-changing musical brims with pressing and universal questions.
Above all, Miranda has created an invigorating and original musical that, at a time of national crisis, celebrates America’s overwhelming debt to the immigrant.
This is obviously a magnificent achievement that on no account is to be missed.
Hamilton is a touchstone. It's zeitgeist, youthquake, Momentum, it's woke, it's post-musical.
It really is as good as we’ve been told.
If anything – and I’m truly sorry to say this
Hamilton expands your heart and concentrates your brain by deliciously stretching your ears.
“Hamilton,” it seems — especially as led by its incendiary newborn star, Mr. Westman — can make a traitor of any English citizen for a night.
Miranda’s sensational score feels ferociously fresh to British ears and his progressive political message is rapturously received.
It’s Miranda’s score that sings, his lyrics that land and Hamilton’s story that stirs.
Even though Hamilton then is preaching to the converted, it is still a dazzlingly inventive piece of musical theatre.
It’s a great show because it’s a great piece of writing.
If anything, it is slightly better than I thought it might be – a heart-breaking work of staggering genius that changes the form of musical theatre for ever.
Read our five-star review of Hamilton at the Victoria Palace Theatre. This review refers to the original cast, including Jamael Westman and Giles Terera.
Black Lives Matter must be hopping mad with this musical.
America’s early history comes alive as never before.
Sell everything you own to get your hands on a ticket.
The gift of Hamilton the musical is that this would-be history lesson is so full of energy and character, lyrical dexterity and subversive humour that there is never any danger of nodding off.
This musical still feels like one of the artistic wonders of the world
You needn’t know who Hamilton is to be swept up in Miranda’s deliciously rich storytelling.
Hamilton is in itself a revolution.

Those who know what they like, like what they know and are sure that hip hop isn’t their thing will only have themselves to blame for missing a show that feels as if it has moved the musical form on and up a notch or two.

cn.t: Critics hail Hamilton as a knockout that transcends its American subject matter, with most praising Miranda's groundbreaking hip-hop musical as revolutionary theater featuring superb performances, particularly from Westman and Terera.
